## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Tilamuṭṭhijātaka* (Ja 252) is a narrative included in the canonical *Jātaka* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. According to the traditional nidāna preserved in the text and commentary, the Buddha delivered the sermon at the Jetavana monastery concerning a monk who was prone to anger, bitterness, and rough speech whenever he was reprimanded [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. The opening verse incipit is *Ajjāpi me taṃ manasīti* [Fausböll 1879]. In the story's identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that the irascible king in the tale of the past was the passionate monk, while he himself was the wise teacher (*ācariya*) [Fausböll 1879].
The prose narrative of the story is notable in discussions of ancient Indian educational customs [Scharfe 2002]. As Hartmut Scharfe observes, the prose elaborations describe non-paying students (*dhammantevāsika*) who performed domestic labor in a teacher's household during the day and acquired their craft through lessons at night [Scharfe 2002]. While A. S. Altekar cited this text as evidence for systematic night classes for poor students, Scharfe emphasizes that these prose sections reflect late traditions fixed in writing in Sri Lanka rather than canonical stratum [Scharfe 2002]. The story has also persisted as a popular instructional text in traditional Sri Lankan Buddhist curricula [Gombrich 1991].
SuttaCentral records no curated parallels in external Buddhist traditions for this Jātaka [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus detects four shared passages solely within the Pali tradition, matching the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Dutiyo bhāgo), with the most extensive alignment encompassing segments 0.4–2.4 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus finds no cross-language matches in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections meeting the reporting threshold [DharmaNexus].
